meta.titre: Word Processing Formatting: shaping text, paragraphs and pages
meta.sous_theme: Character, paragraph and page formatting in a word processor

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L Computer Science past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: A secretary at a school in Bamenda has typed a notice for parents, but the page looks untidy: the heading sits on the left, the lines are crowded and no page number appears. In a few clicks she can fix all of this. Word processing questions in the GCE come in two forms. The multiple-choice paper asks you to name a tool or a feature, and the practical paper asks you to open a file, format it as instructed and save it. The marks go to those who know exactly which feature does which job.

items: A word processor is a program used to type, edit, format, save and print documents.
A paragraph is a block of text that ends when you press the Enter key.
Text must be selected (highlighted) before a format can be applied to it.
A file must be saved with a name before the computer is switched off.

sections.titre: Formatting a document at character, paragraph and page level
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Editing and formatting

**Editing** changes the content of a document: you type, delete, copy, move or correct words. **Formatting** changes only how the document looks, not what it says. To format text that is already typed, **select it first** (highlight it with the mouse), then choose the feature.

### Three levels of formatting

| Level | What it controls | Common features |
|---|---|---|
| Character | The look of letters | Font type, font size (in points), bold, italic, underline, font colour, change case |
| Paragraph | A block of text that ends when you press Enter | Alignment (left, centre, right, justified), line spacing (single, 1.5, double), indent, bullets and numbering |
| Page | The whole sheet | Margins, orientation, paper size, header and footer, page numbers |

A justified paragraph has straight edges on both the left and the right. A heading is usually centred, bold and larger than the body text.

### Page setup

A **margin** is the empty space between the text and the edge of the paper. You can set the top, bottom, left and right margins separately. **Orientation** is either **portrait** (the page is taller than it is wide) or **landscape** (the page is wider than it is tall). A4 paper measures 21 cm by 29.7 cm in portrait, so the width of the writing area is:

text width = page width - left margin - right margin

and the height of the writing area is found in the same way with the top and bottom margins. A **header** is text repeated at the top of every page and a **footer** is text repeated at the bottom; page numbers are normally inserted in one of them.

### Proofing tools

- The **spell checker** marks words that are not in its dictionary.
- The **grammar checker** marks sentences that may be built wrongly.
- The **thesaurus** gives synonyms, which are words with a similar meaning.
- **Find and Replace** looks for a word or phrase and changes every match.

A spell checker cannot see that a correctly spelled word is the wrong word, such as *their* typed in place of *there*, so always read your work again.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the task names a heading, a paragraph or some words
variantes.contenu_markdown: Select exactly the text named in the task, then apply each feature one by one: for example a centred, bold, 18 point heading needs alignment, bold and font size. Check on screen that the next paragraph has not changed by accident.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the task gives margins, orientation or a header or footer
variantes.contenu_markdown: Open the page setup options (in Microsoft Word, the Layout or Page Layout tab), type the margin values in cm for all four sides and pick portrait or landscape. For a page number, open the footer or header, then insert the page number field instead of typing a number by hand.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the task says to save the file under a new name
variantes.contenu_markdown: **Save** keeps the same file name and overwrites the old version. **Save As** lets you choose a new name, folder or file type. If a task says to save the opened file with a new name, use Save As so that the original file is left unchanged.

sections.enonce_markdown:
A word processing file named **Sports Day Notice** is open. Follow these instructions.

- Set all four margins to 2 cm and the page orientation to landscape on A4 paper.
- Format the heading *Inter-House Sports* as centred, bold, 18 point.
- Format the body paragraph as justified with line spacing 1.5.
- Insert the page number in the footer.
- Work out the width and the height of the writing area, then save the file as **Task 2**.

etapes.justification: Margins and orientation affect where every line falls, so setting them first avoids reformatting later.
etapes.resultat_markdown: All four margins = 2 cm; orientation = landscape.

etapes.action: Work out the writing area for landscape A4.
etapes.justification: In landscape the 29.7 cm side becomes the width and the 21 cm side becomes the height.

etapes.action: Select the heading and format it.
etapes.justification: Character and paragraph features act on the selected text only.

etapes.action: Select the body paragraph and format it.
etapes.justification: Justify makes both edges straight and the line spacing option sets the gap between lines.

etapes.action: Insert the page number in the footer, then use Save As.
etapes.justification: A page number field changes automatically on every page, and Save As gives the file its new name.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Footer contains the page number; file saved as Task 2.

sections.conclusion_markdown: The page is landscape with margins of 2 cm. The writing area is **25.7 cm wide and 17.0 cm high**. The heading is centred, bold and 18 point, the paragraph is justified with 1.5 spacing, the footer carries the page number and the file is saved as Task 2.

items.erreur_markdown: Centring a heading by pressing the space bar many times before the first word.
items.pourquoi_faux: Spaces only push the text from the left. The heading moves again as soon as the font, size or margin changes, and it is rarely truly centred.
items.correction_markdown: Select the heading and use the **centre alignment** button.

items.erreur_markdown: Pressing Enter at the end of every line while typing a paragraph.
items.pourquoi_faux: A word processor wraps text automatically at the right margin. Pressing Enter at each line end creates many small paragraphs, so justify, line spacing and margins behave badly when the text is edited.
items.correction_markdown: Keep typing so the text wraps by itself, and press Enter only at the end of a paragraph.

items.erreur_markdown: Using the spell checker to find a word with a similar meaning, or the thesaurus to correct a misspelled word.
items.pourquoi_faux: The two tools have different jobs. The spell checker checks spelling and the thesaurus only offers synonyms.
items.correction_markdown: Spelling: **spell checker**. Words of similar meaning: **thesaurus**.

items.erreur_markdown: Saying that landscape means the page is taller than it is wide.
items.pourquoi_faux: This is the meaning of portrait. A landscape page is wider than it is tall, like a picture of a wide view.
items.correction_markdown: Portrait: height greater than width. **Landscape: width greater than height**.

items.erreur_markdown: Clicking Save on an opened file when the task says to save it with a new name.
items.pourquoi_faux: Save writes over the original file under the old name, so the unformatted version is lost and the new name is never created.
items.correction_markdown: Use **Save As**, type the new name and confirm the folder.

items.enonce_markdown:
Name the word processing feature that does each job.

(a) Offers other words with a meaning similar to *big*.
(b) Underlines the misspelled word *recieve* and suggests a correction.
(c) Changes every *Form 4* in a long document into *Form 5* in one operation.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) The **thesaurus**. It lists synonyms.

(b) The **spell checker**. It compares each word with its dictionary.

(c) **Find and Replace**. It finds every match of the first phrase and replaces it with the second.

items.enonce_markdown:
A4 paper is 21 cm wide and 29.7 cm high in portrait. A typist sets the left and right margins to 3 cm and the top and bottom margins to 2.5 cm.

(a) Find the width and height of the writing area in portrait.
(b) The typist changes the orientation to landscape and keeps the same margins. Find the new width and height of the writing area.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) Portrait: width = 21 - 3 - 3 = **15.0 cm**; height = 29.7 - 2.5 - 2.5 = **24.7 cm**.

(b) Landscape: the page is 29.7 cm wide and 21 cm high. Width = 29.7 - 3 - 3 = **23.7 cm**; height = 21 - 2.5 - 2.5 = **16.0 cm**.

The margins keep their sides (left, right, top, bottom), so the left and right margins now take space from the longer side.

items.enonce_markdown:
A student must prepare a two-page report using these instructions.

- Title centred, bold, 16 point; body text justified with double line spacing.
- All four margins 2.5 cm on A4 portrait.
- Page numbers at the bottom of each page.
- Save the file as **Report**.

(a) Write the tasks in a sensible order, naming the tool or option used for each.
(b) Calculate the area of the writing area in portrait.
(c) The student switches to landscape with the same margins. Calculate the new area and comment.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) Award a mark for each correct task: 1. Open page setup, set all four margins to 2.5 cm, keep portrait A4. 2. Type the text. 3. Select the title, then use centre alignment, bold and font size 16. 4. Select the body, then use justify and double line spacing. 5. Open the footer and insert the page number. 6. Check the spelling with the spell checker. 7. Use Save As and name the file Report.

(b) Portrait: width = 21 - 2.5 - 2.5 = 16.0 cm; height = 29.7 - 2.5 - 2.5 = 24.7 cm. Area = 16.0 x 24.7 = **395.2 square cm**.

(c) Landscape: width = 29.7 - 2.5 - 2.5 = 24.7 cm; height = 21 - 2.5 - 2.5 = 16.0 cm. Area = 24.7 x 16.0 = **395.2 square cm**. The area is the same because the same two lengths are multiplied; only the shape of the writing area changes.

items_markdown: Editing changes the content of a document; formatting changes its appearance. Select text before formatting it.
Formatting works at three levels: character (font, size, bold), paragraph (alignment, line spacing, bullets) and page (margins, orientation, header and footer).
Portrait is taller than wide and landscape is wider than tall. On A4, text width = page width - left margin - right margin.
Use the spell checker for spelling, the thesaurus for synonyms and Find and Replace to change every match of a word.
Let text wrap by itself and press Enter only at the end of a paragraph; use alignment buttons, not the space bar, to position text.
Use Save As to give a file a new name and keep the original unchanged.
